description:
Architecture seams of an imported repository: a DISTINCT axis from risk — not "where is
the code fragile?" but "where does the code fight its own structure?". A seam is a source of
truth split across module boundaries: files in different packages that keep being edited
together over the history (e.g. the same list enumerated in two packages). Read from the
co-change history alone, scored by near-inseparability (jaccard) with a hub penalty, so
wanted shared contracts (api-types/dto/schema...) are listed apart, never counted as debt.
Each seam carries its evidence (shared identifiers, co-commits, span) and a confidence; the
tool proposes, it does not decide — a seam is not a bug and never appears in the risk axis.
`scope` = actionable (default) | all | expected; `min_jaccard` filters weaker seams; `zone`
(path prefix or words) narrows to seams touching that zone. Backed by a retrospective bench
(backtest_coupling): on the reference repo a flagged seam predicts future co-change with a
lift of several times over a random previously-coupled pair.
name: hokmah_seams
title: Architecture Seams (what to refactor)
